nodes.description: Biallelic loss-of-function COA6 variants remove a small twin-CX9C intermembrane-space protein whose coiled-coil-helix-coiled-coil-helix fold is redox-active. COA6 reduces the copper-coordinating disulfides of its client proteins SCO1 and COX2, which is what permits copper binding in the oxidizing intermembrane space. On the best-supported reading this node is a failure to prepare the copper-accepting cysteines rather than a failure to deliver copper. That reading is not unanimous: COA6 binds copper in vitro, a crystal structure assigns one of its disulfides a likely copper-binding site, and a metallochaperone role has also been proposed. See the discussion attached to this node.

nodes.description: An investigational, mechanism-directed lead rather than an established therapy. Because the lesion is a failure to prepare copper-accepting cysteines, raising available copper partially bypasses it in cell and yeast models. The two published results differ in system and in magnitude and should not be merged: copper completely rescued respiratory and assembly defects in yeast coa6-null cells, and gave only a partial rescue in patient fibroblasts. No administration to a COA6 patient has been reported, and no clinical efficacy is claimed here.

nodes.description: Deficient cytochrome c oxidase cannot accept electrons from cytochrome c and pass them to molecular oxygen, so the terminal step of the respiratory chain and its coupled proton pumping fail. Whether the enzyme defect is confined to Complex IV is contested: the index patient was reported with isolated Complex IV deficiency, while a COA6 knockout cell line showed combined Complex I and Complex IV loss. See the discussion attached to this node.
